# Opus V3 Integrated Revision (Parent V2): Researcher-Assisted Modern Feedback Round

## Status and provenance

This is a modern, researcher-assisted revision. It is not part of the original 1898 concept, and none of the course material or later theory below was in the original packet. Every value carries one of three labels:

- **ASSUMPTION**: a design choice or assumed value.
- **EXT-CALC**: an independent evaluator calculation that was supplied to me.
- **DESIGN-EST**: my own arithmetic on assumed shapes and masses.

**No measured results exist.** Nothing here gives construction or crewed-flight clearance.

## 1. Changes from V2 and three-view schedule

**Changes from V2**

| ID | Item | V2 | V3 | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Propeller data (adopted from V6) | radius 1.2 m, rpm UNKNOWN, ratio UNKNOWN | D 2.4 m, 2 blades, 400 rpm, 2.5:1 chain (engine 1000 rpm), rotation +x̂ (anticlockwise viewed from behind) | Mechanically compatible: same disc at x=2.1, same hub. Blade chords S1–S3 and S5–S8 are still missing, so there is no thrust claim. |
| D2 | V6 blade sections V4/V5A | not present | Recorded only; not adopted as performance | V5A is unscreened. V4 has a sharp trailing edge that cannot be built. |
| D3 | Ventral fin T5 | none | 0.8 × 0.35 m (0.28 m²), x 4.8–5.6, z 0.25–0.60, 0.8 kg | Fin volume rises from ~0.020 to ~0.023. Clearance at 13° rotation is 0.221 m. |
| D4 | Pitch-trim bungee K3 | none | Adjustable spring on the column, 0.5 kg | Lets the pilot relieve stick force when the thrust moment changes between power-on and power-off. |
| D5 | Fuel split | E3 15 kg, one item | E3a tank 3 kg + E3b fuel 12 kg (~16 L) | Allows the empty-fuel CG extreme to be computed. |
| D6 | Pilot envelope | 70 kg fixed | 70–90 kg; seat ballast brings any lighter pilot up to 70 kg | Bounds the aft CG. |
| D7 | Intrinsic inertia | UNKNOWN | Shape and dimension for every item | Evaluator request. |
| D8 | Mass and CG | 360 kg, (0.6148, 0, 0.4609) | 361.3 kg, (0.6227, 0, 0.4601) | Result of D3 and D4. |

**Rejected options (retained for the record)**

- V5A blade sections adopted as a performance basis.
- Choosing a static-margin target on its own.
- Raising dihedral now. This is held as a contingency in Section 7.
- A ventral fin down to z 0.10. Rejected because it leaves only 0.074 m clearance at 13° rotation.

**Three-view coordinates**

Origin is the lower-wing leading edge on the centreline. Axes: x aft, y starboard, z up.

- **Lower wing:** leading edge x 0, chord 1.8, span ±5.5. Flat to |y| 1.6, then 1° dihedral to a tip z of 0.0681.
- **Upper wing:** z 1.8 at root, tip z 1.8681.
- **Tailplane:** leading edge x 4.5, z 0.6, span ±2.2.
- **Elevator hinge:** x 5.6, TE at x 6.1.
- **Fin:** leading edge x 4.8, z 0.6–2.0.
- **Rudder hinge:** x 5.6, z 0.68–2.0.
- **Ventral fin:** x 4.8–5.6, z 0.25–0.60.
- **Propeller disc:** x 2.1, centre (2.1, 0, 0.9), radius 1.2.
- **Nacelle:** x −1.6 to 0.2.
- **Skids:** tips at (−1.9, ±0.95, −0.55), flat run x −1.5 to 1.6 at z −0.9.
- **Tail skid tip:** (5.5, 0, 0.0).
- **Ground:** z −0.9 at rest.

## 2. Mass ledger, extremes and inertia

**Conventions**

- Inertia: Ixx=∫(y²+z²)dm, Iyy=∫(x²+z²)dm, Izz=∫(x²+y²)dm.
- Product: Ixz=∫xz dm. The tensor off-diagonal entry is −Ixz.
- Moments L, M, N follow the right-hand rule about +x (aft), +y (starboard) and +z (up).
  - Positive q is nose-up.
  - Positive p (about the aft axis) raises the starboard wing, i.e. a left roll.
  - Positive r turns the nose to port.
- Mapping to standard stability axes (x forward, y starboard, z down) uses T=diag(−1, 1, −1): p_s=−p, q_s=q, r_s=−r. Ixz is unchanged by this mapping.

**Items and properties**

The full ledger is in the JSON. All masses are ASSUMPTIONS, and none has been weighed. Intrinsic inertias are DESIGN-EST for uniform idealised shapes. The seated human modelled as a uniform box is a crude approximation, and its true inertia is UNKNOWN.

**Totals (nominal state: 70 kg pilot, full fuel)**

- Mass 361.3 kg.
- Σx = 224.975 kg·m, Σz = 166.223 kg·m.
- CG = (0.6227, 0, 0.4601).

**Extremes**

| State | Mass (kg) | CG (x, z) |
|---|---|---|
| 70 kg pilot, empty fuel (aft limit) | 349.3 | (0.6269, 0.4553) |
| 90 kg pilot, full fuel (forward limit) | 381.3 | (0.5428, 0.4517) |
| 90 kg pilot, empty fuel | 369.3 | (0.5442, 0.4469) |

**Whole-aircraft inertia (DESIGN-EST, not measured)**

The whole-aircraft values below come from a parallel-axis sum plus the intrinsic terms. The evaluator must recompute them from the ledger.

| Quantity | Value (kg·m²) | Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Iyy | ≈1030 | ±25% |
| Ixx | ≈1100 | ±30% |
| Izz | ≈1800 | ±30% |
| Ixz | ≈+80 | ±60% |

- Ixy and Iyz are zero by assumed symmetry.
- **Propeller angular momentum:** h = Ip·ω = 4.43 × 41.89 ≈ 186 kg·m²/s along +x.
- **Resolving test:** weigh each component. Suspend the whole aircraft at two or more points to find the CG. Swing it as a bifilar or compound pendulum about three axes plus one skewed axis to obtain Ixz.

## 3. Installed surfaces and controls

**Elevator**

- Hinge from (5.6, −2.2, 0.6) to (5.6, 2.2, 0.6).
- Travel −15° to +20°, positive = TE up = nose-up.
- Linkage sense: column aft gives TE up.
- TE vertical sweep z 0.471–0.771.

**Balancing flaps**

- Hinges run from (1.35, ±3.5, 1.884) to (1.35, ±5.5, 1.919). Travel ±15°, opposed.
- Linkage sense: wheel right gives starboard TE up and port TE down, which rolls right.
- Adverse yaw is UNKNOWN.

**Rudder**

- Hinge from (5.6, 0, 0.68) to (5.6, 0, 2.0). Travel ±25°.
- Positive = TE to port = nose right. Linkage sense: right pedal forward.
- Rudder bottom is 0.06 m above the torque tube.

**Ventral fin**

- Fixed surface.
- Clearance to the tail skid braces (G4) must be checked on a mock-up.

**Rate limits**

Rate limits are an ASSUMPTION of manual-cable capability: 60°/s for elevator and rudder, 45°/s for the flaps. They are UNKNOWN. The resolving test is a bench cable rig with measured stretch, friction, backlash and deflection versus time under a simulated hinge load.

**Hinge moments**

Hinge moments are UNKNOWN. The resolving test is a tow or wind-tunnel measurement with a hinge balance.

**Body and propeller as installed**

- Nacelle: box 1.8 × 0.7 × 0.75 m.
- Propeller: pusher disc at x 2.1. It lies 0.22 m behind the wing TE and 0.383 m from the upper boom spar.
- Tail surfaces lie partly in the slipstream. The size of that effect is UNKNOWN.

## 4. Propulsion, drag and trim

**Operating point (15 m/s)**

The EXT-CALC demand of 11.67 kW against an unverified 13 kW target implies a required installed efficiency of 0.576. DESIGN-EST values at T = 448 N:

- Advance ratio J = V/(nD) = 0.9375.
- Thrust coefficient CT = 0.248.
- Power coefficient CP at 13 kW = 0.450.
- Momentum-ideal efficiency ≈ 0.86.
- Tip helical speed ≈ 52 m/s.

Engine power and propeller efficiency are both UNKNOWN. This requires an engine brake test and a propeller stand-plus-tow test.

**Drag scenarios**

Nominal CD0 = 0.050 on Sref, i.e. 261 N parasite drag plus 185 N induced drag.

| Scenario | Parasite drag | Shaft power at η 0.576 |
|---|---|---|
| Low | −30% | ≈9.6 kW |
| Nominal | nominal | ≈11.67 kW |
| High | +30% | ≈13.7 kW |

The high case exceeds the unverified 13 kW target.

**Trim strategy**

- The thrust line (z 0.9) is about 0.44 m above the CG, so thrust produces a moment of ≈ −0.44·T N·m (nose-down).
- At power-off this nose-down moment is removed. The change is ≈ +197 N·m nose-up at 15 m/s.
- Holding the same speed therefore needs ≈1.9° more TE-down elevator, assuming Cmδ ≈ 0.011/deg ±50%.
- The bungee is preset to the power-off glide. Power-on stick force is then held manually. Magnitudes are UNKNOWN.
- Power-on and power-off trim must be solved by the evaluator at each state listed in Section 5.

## 5. Derivative analysis and test matrix

**Test states**

- Speeds 13, 15 and 18 m/s. The 13 m/s case applies only if a stall estimate shows margin.
- CG positions: forward 0.5428, nominal 0.6227, aft 0.6269.
- Power: on (T = D) and off (windmill or idle).
- This gives 18 cases.

**Derivatives required**

- **Longitudinal:** CX_u, CX_α, CZ_u, CZ_α, CZ_q, CZ_α̇, Cm_u, Cm_α, Cm_q, Cm_α̇.
- **Lateral:** CY_β, CY_p, CY_r, Cl_β, Cl_p, Cl_r, Cn_β, Cn_p, Cn_r.
- **Control:** CZ, Cm and CX with respect to δe; Cl, Cn and CY with respect to δf and δr.
- **Propulsion:** T_u, T_δthrottle, the thrust moment arm, propeller normal force versus α and β (P-factor), slipstream increments on the tail, and the gyroscopic h.

**Methods**

1. **Steady derivatives:** AVL or VLM on the V3 geometry with the biplane cellule, nacelle and boom bodies (slender body), plus fin and ventral fin. The evaluator runs this.
2. **Unsteady CL_α̇ and Cm_α̇:** these must NOT be taken from steady AVL.
   - First estimate: the tail downwash-lag formula, Cm_α̇ ≈ −2·a_t·η_t·V_H·(l_t/c)·dε/dα. The inputs dε/dα and a_t come from VLM. The result is an ESTIMATE only.
   - Resolution: a captive-model forced-oscillation test (pitch and plunge separation), or an unsteady panel or frequency-domain model.
3. **Control and slipstream effects:** tow or wind-tunnel tests of a model with the propeller running.
4. **Uncertainty:** each derivative gets a ± band. Absent values stay UNKNOWN and are never set to zero.

## 6. Longitudinal and lateral roots

**Calculation path**

- Longitudinal state [u, w, q, θ]; lateral state [v, p, r, φ].
- Dimensional derivatives use the ledger mass and the Section 2 inertias, with Ixz retained.
- Gyroscopic coupling from h adds a moment of (0, −r·h, +q·h) in the body frame. It couples the two 4×4 blocks, so an 8×8 coupled solution must also be run.
- Run a Monte Carlo sweep over the derivative and inertia bands and report root clouds.

**Mode labels**

- Longitudinal: phugoid (2 roots) and short period (2 roots).
- Lateral: roll subsidence, spiral, and Dutch roll (2 roots).

**Screening estimates (DESIGN-EST, not verdicts)**

- **Lanchester phugoid:** ω ≈ √2·g/V = 0.92 rad/s (period ≈ 6.8 s), ζ ≈ 0.09.
  - This ignores Cm_u and thrust effects, so its stability is UNKNOWN.
- **Reduced short period:** uses the EXT-CALC determinant with Iyy ≈ 1030 kg·m². Result: ω ≈ 3.8 rad/s, ζ ≈ 0.9.
  - This excludes Mα̇, u-coupling and propulsion, and the value may change substantially.
- **Lateral roots:** all UNKNOWN.

## 7. Contingency if a mode is unstable

The ventral fin raises Cn_β, which may worsen the spiral mode.

**If the spiral mode diverges with a doubling time under 10 s, or the Dutch roll has ζ < 0.05, increase outer-panel dihedral from 1° to 2.5°.**

- **Geometry:** tip rise changes from 0.068 m to 0.170 m. Outer strut and wire lengths are recut.
- **Mass:** about +0.3 kg; CG change is negligible.
- **Aerodynamics:** lift loss about 0.1%. Cl_β becomes more negative, which may reduce Dutch-roll damping, so the roots must be re-solved.
- **Trim and power:** trim is essentially unchanged; power rises by less than 1%.
- **Ground clearance:** wingtip roll contact improves from 11.9° to about 12.8°.

**If the aft-CG phugoid or short period is unstable:** limit the aft CG with 5 kg of fixed ballast at x = −1.4.

- CG shifts forward by ≈0.03 m.
- Elevator trim moves TE-up by ≈0.5°.
- Required power rises by ≈1.5%.

## 8. Unresolved items and stop/go criteria

**Unresolved**

- Engine existence and power curve.
- Propeller chords, stacking axis and polars, including confirmation of the V6 rotation hand.
- Section stall.
- Parasite drag.
- All installed derivatives.
- α̇ and slipstream terms.
- Measured inertias.
- Hinge moments and cable dynamics.
- Structural allowables.
- Flexibility.
- The evaluator elevator-sign mapping.

**Stop/go gates**

These are gates for the next analysis step only, not for flight.

1. The mass and inertia ledger is recomputed independently and agrees within 5%.
2. Every state in the matrix trims power-on and power-off within control limits, keeping at least 25% of control travel in reserve.
3. All eight roots across the uncertainty sweep meet all of these conditions:
   - Real parts ≤ 0.
   - Spiral doubling time ≥ 10 s, if it is divergent.
   - Short-period and Dutch-roll ζ ≥ 0.1.
4. Measured engine power is at least the high-drag requirement plus 15%.
5. A proof load and ground/tow test plan is reviewed.

**If any gate fails, stop and revise.**
